plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid in a first-price auction is (n-1)/n times my value, i.e., (2/3)*value. This balances winning probability against overpaying. My value is $14, so I'll bid approximately $9.30 to maximize expected profit while remaining competitive.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3. My value is $34, so optimal bid ≈ 34 × (2/3) ≈ 22.7. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitive against other rational bidders using similar strategies.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, which for n=3 is 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $33, so I'll bid approximately $22 to optimize expected profit, avoiding overpaying while maintaining a competitive chance of winning.
